subject: Normal distribution with mean = 7000 and ranges from 3000 to 11000

messages.author: 45cb335aaa1f534b
messages.subject: Normal distribution with mean = 7000 and ranges from 3000 to 11000
parts:
Dear All,
 
I've tried to draw a normal distribution, with mean = 7000, and x-axis from 3000 to 11000, with an area from 7000 to 8000 in grey colour. I have not success though.
 
Would be appreciate if anyone can help!
 
Best regards,
Trong

messages.author: 13ff1921a4b26560
messages.subject: Re: Normal distribution with mean = 7000 and ranges from 3000 to 11000
parts:
Hi Trong,
  you didn't specify a standard deviation for your normal distribution and I'm not precisely sure what you mean about the area in colour - sharing code of what you have tried can be helpful.
Here is code that shows both how to plot a normal distribution and how to generate a dataframe that outlines an arbitrary polygon (shown with grey fill which is what I think you want). Hope this helps! See also:
?stat_function
-Allan


library(ggplot2)

# points for a polygon that starts and ends on x-axis
mydata <- data.frame(x = c(7000, 7000:8000, 8000))
mydata$y <- dnorm(mydata$x, mean = 7000, sd = 1000)
mydata$y[1] <- 0
mydata$y[nrow(mydata)] <- 0

# overlay a function and a predefined polygon
# with grey fill on a white background
ggplot(data.frame(x = c(3000, 11000)), aes(x)) +
  geom_polygon(data = mydata, aes(x, y), fill = "grey") +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, arg = list(mean = 7000, sd = 1000)) +
  theme_bw()

#  R version 3.0.1 (2013-05-16) Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit) 
# ggplot2_0.9.3.1

Dear Allan,

 

Your code does precisely what I need. Thank you very much indeed!

 

Since I’ve problem with a normal distribution that the mean differs from zero, I could only do:

 

x=seq(-3,3, length=200)

y=dnorm(x)

par(bty='n')

plot(x,y,type="l", lwd=3, col="black", xlab="",

                ylab="", main="",

                xaxt="n", yaxt="n")

x=seq(0,1, length=200)

y=dnorm(x)

polygon(c(0,x,1),c(0,y,0),col="gray")

 

When I tried to alter the range, e.g. from 3000 to 11000, then I stuck.

 

Thanks again!

 

Best regards,

Trong
